hints.content:
$f$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals h of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, negative twelve and it decreases through the point negative four, negative fifty. It continues to decrease until the local minimum at negative two and one-half, negative sixty-five. Then it increases through the point negative one, negative fifty, the y-intercept zero, negative thirty, and the point one, negative five. It increases until the local maximum at two and one-half, twelve. Then it decreases through the x-intercept four, zero and the point five, negative forty. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative two and one-half to x equals two and one-half.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4<x<-3$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is decreasing on this interval
$-2<x<-1$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$0<x<1$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
